1import logging 

2 

3import torch 

4 

5logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

6 

7 

8def _nested_view_from_buffer_copy( 

9 self: torch.Tensor, 

10 nested_size: torch.Tensor, 

11 nested_strides: torch.Tensor, 

12 offsets: torch.Tensor, 

13): 

14 logger.debug("GEMS_CAMBRICON _NESTED_VIEW_FROM_BUFFER_COPY") 

15 

16 # The Cambricon (mlu) NestedTensor backend does not implement several ops 

17 # (e.g. aten::unbind.int, aten::_to_copy), so a nested tensor built directly 

18 # on the device is unusable and torch.nested.nested_tensor on device tensors 

19 # also fails. In addition, torch.nested.nested_tensor under use_gems would 

20 # dispatch through the Cambricon cat/vstack path. 

21 # 

22 # Workaround: extract each component on device using as_strided, move the 

23 # (small, contiguous) components to CPU, and assemble the nested tensor on 

24 # CPU where unbind and the rest of the nested API are fully supported. 

25 num_components = nested_size.shape[0] 

26 components = [] 

27 

28 for i in range(num_components): 

29 size_i = int(nested_size[i].item()) 

30 stride_i = int(nested_strides[i].item()) 

31 offset_i = int(offsets[i].item()) 

32 

33 # Extract component and clone to obtain contiguous memory before the 

34 # host copy. 

35 component = self.as_strided((size_i,), (stride_i,), offset_i).clone().cpu() 

36 components.append(component) 

37 

38 result = torch.nested.nested_tensor(components) 

39 return result
